title: reading-cascade-notes-llm-refinement
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick personal scratchpad summarizing a small reading sprint + thoughts on building a lightweight cascaded pipeline for long-context refinement (notes for the 4/17 sync).
- Goal: practical heuristics we can test quickly on Redwood workloads (search+LLM rerank + multi-pass condensation) rather than a full research paper.

Key takeaway themes (high level):
1) Cascade as an engineering pattern: cheap upstream filters -> mid-cost rerankers -> expensive contextual generator. Tune thresholds for recall vs cost.
2) Multi-pass refinement beats single-shot for noisy long inputs: extractive pass -> compression -> generative consolidation.
3) Prefix/KV cache and chunking interplay: memory cost grows with chunking; reusing cache between adjacent chunks can reduce duplicate compute but must handle context boundary artifacts.

Papers and quick notes (one-liners):
- "Progressive Retrieval for Long Documents" (notes): progressive retrieval (coarse->fine) seems directly applicable; use dense retrieval for recall then lexical for precision. Open Q: thresholding heuristics? use model confidence (~logit gap) + retrieval similarity.
- "Two-stage Summarization with Compression Models" (blog + arXiv): compression model that outputs dense summary tokens (200-300) and then generate. Good ablation on error propagation.
- "Token Merging (ToMe) and Compute-aware Attention": idea: apply soft merging for earlier layers in coarse pass to reduce token count. Could try cheap quantized model for first pass.
- "Sliding-window KV caching for long-context models" (workshop slides): important to avoid naive re-population when window slides; maintain rolling cache with chunk overlap of 32-128 tokens.

Hands-on recipe (for next two sprints):
- Data: pick 2 workloads from Analytics + Conversational support: (A) long product manuals -> question answering, (B) multi-turn support logs -> condensed summaries. 150 examples each.
- Pipeline candidates:
  A) Baseline: single-shot Llama2-70b-8bit on 8k window (costly).
  B) Cascade-v1: dense retrieval -> 1st-pass cheap summarizer (quantized Llama-7B) -> 2nd-pass generator (32k context).
  C) Cascade-v2: lexical + dense hybrid retrieval -> chunk-level compression (50-200 tokens) -> consolidation with function-calling template to preserve structured fields.
- Metrics: latency p50/p95, tokens billed, ROUGE/QA-accuracy, human eval quality (3-pt scale), failure modes (hallucination rate).

Micro-implementation notes / heuristics:
- Retrieval thresholding: set recall-oriented threshold for dense retrieval (0.65) then run lexical similarity filter (fuzzy overlap) to remove obviously irrelevant docs.
- Compression proxy: train a small finetune to map chunk -> compressed snippet using a high-precision loss (KL to teacher generation). If not enough time, use an extractive heuristic (lead-3 + TF-IDF salient spans).
- Cache reuse: when chunk i and chunk i+1 overlap by 64 tokens, preserve last 2 layer KV slices for overlap region; evict fine-grained portions for previous chunks to keep memory bounded. This needs runtime support (see infra notes).
- Model selection policy: cheap quantized models for recall/compression, higher precision float models for consolidation. Route by token budget and latency SLO.

Quick infra TODOs (practical constraints):
- Talk to infra (SRE) about pinned GPU pools for experimental runs to avoid preemption noise (ticket RI-987).
- Add a flag in the runtime to allow explicit KV-slice-save for chunk overlaps (small API change on serving runtime).
- Instrument per-token model breakdown in console so we can attribute cost to each cascade stage.

Open questions / experiments to prioritize:
1) How sensitive is human-perceived answer quality to compression size? Sweep compression length 50/100/200/400 tokens.
2) Does overlapping KV cache produce boundary hallucinations? Measure hallucination rate near chunk boundaries vs internal answer regions.
3) Can we use model internal confidence to auto-stop cascade (i.e., if generator's top token prob > threshold, skip consolidation)?
4) Cost fallback strategy: if consolidation fails (timeout or OOM), degrade gracefully to compressed extractive answer and mark provenance.

Notes to self / heuristics I want to record:
- When in doubt, prefer extra recall at retrieval stage; downstream compression can remove noise but lost recall is irreversible.
- Use a simple human-facing tag structure for outputs: [EXTRACTIVE], [REFINED], [SUSPECT-HALLUCINATION] to speed triage in human eval.

Meeting prep for 4/17 sync (agenda bullets):
- 5 min: sprint goals and datasets (A+B).
- 10 min: proposed pipeline diagrams (v1/v2) + cost/latency estimates.
- 10 min: infra changes needed (KV-slice API, pinned GPUs).
- 10 min: experiment matrix and milestones (week1: retrieval+extractive baseline; week2: compression model; week3: consolidation + human eval).
- 5 min: open Q & ownership (assign tasks).

Rough notes / snippets (shorthand, thinking out loud):
- "if cache_overlap > 0.5 * chunk_len then probably reuse slice else recompute" (really heuristic).
- "try 2:1 compute ratio (cheap:expensive) first — i.e., cheap pass 2x more tokens allowed than consolidation)"
- "instrument per-request fallback counter so we can later quantify how often we hit fallbacks in canary runs"

References / links to read first before sync (priority order):
1) Progressive retrieval paper + authors' code (skim; implement minimal retrieval stack)
2) Compression-as-preprocessing blog post (practical heuristics)
3) KV-window/rolling-cache slides (for infra ask)

TODOs (I will own):
- [ ] Prepare synthetic dataset sample (30 examples per workload) by 4/13.
- [ ] Prototype extractive compression heuristic and measure token savings on 20 examples by 4/16.
- [ ] Draft runtime API change proposal for KV-slice reuse and share with infra by 4/18.

Random long-term curiosities (notes):
- Could we learn retrieval thresholds with small RL signal (human accept/reject) rather than rules? Interesting but out of scope for current sprint.
- Combining ToMe-like token merges with retrieval: merge less salient tokens in cheap pass to reduce compute but keep semantic anchors for consolidation.

End of scratchpad.

Notes: this doc is intentionally informal — will iterate into a Confluence design doc if the initial experiments look promising. Save as working notes and link to experiments PRs.
